# #3695: Patch: the AI Floats mana on purpose to bring its Float-discount cards within reach
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Some of the game's biggest cards cost more than anyone can ever have in one turn, and get cheaper each time their owner ends a turn with mana left over (a Float). A human player saves mana on purpose for a turn or two to land a 12/12 Battleship. The practice AI never does, because it scores leftover mana as pure waste, so these cards sit dead in its hand. Once this is built, the AI counts unspent mana as bringing such a card closer, and a player will see it hold back a turn and then drop its giant.

## Why
- Mana caps at 4 (`MAX_MANA`, `crates/engine/src/config.rs:41`; SPEC §2.3). Seven cards carry "Float reduces cost" (`float_reduces_cost`; SPEC §6 Float, R464, R1563000): Drone Core VII to X (5, 6, 6 and 8 mana; `crates/cards/src/scripts/stinkyscape/c033`–`c036`), GIGA Glowy Jelly Bean and Snom Bunny Mind Control (`crates/cards/src/scripts/core/c029`, `c049`) and YileGPT Prime (8 mana, `crates/cards/src/scripts/meditative/c049_1_yilegpt_unleashed.rs`).
- The AI charges `AI_EVAL.unspent_mana` (0.8 a crystal, `crates/ai/src/config.rs:652`) on every passed line (`crates/ai/src/simulate.rs:727`) and after every reply (`crates/ai/src/reply.rs:618`), but prices a discount on a hand card at `hand_cost_delta` (0.5 a crystal, `config.rs:589`, read at `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:562`). With one Float card in hand every crystal Floated scores −0.3, whether or not the discount is what puts the card within reach.
- The hand prices an 8-cost card as a 6-cost one (`hand_cost_cap: 6.0`, `config.rs:582`) whatever the mana cap, so how far a card is from castable never enters the score.
- The sweep shows it. Drone Core X at Hard: drawn in 27 of 58 games, within mana on 18 turns, cast once (`training/history/sweep-2026-10-29-4.md:249`); the day before, within mana on 3 turns of 8 games and never cast (`training/history/sweep-2026-10-28.md:42`). `crates/ai/tests/ai/shadow_ban.rs:514-516` notes that Easy never brings GIGA Glowy Jelly Bean down to its four crystals by Floating.

## Proposal
- An engine read, in `crates/engine/src/query.rs` with its test (CLAUDE.md, Architecture: a missing board fact goes into the engine), of what a Float of n would take off each of a seat's hand cards, read from their hand triggers.
- A new weight, `AI_EVAL.float_discount`, pricing each crystal a line's Float takes off a hand card that still costs more than the seat's crystals. It starts at or above `unspent_mana`, stays 0 in `GREEDY_EVAL`, and goes through the gate like any weight change.
- The sweep's second number, 18 turns within mana and one cast, may have a second cause. A decision test with Drone Core X in reach and a free unit zone finds it: fixed here if small, reported in the pull request if not.

## Where it lands
- `crates/engine/src/query.rs` (or `float.rs`), `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`, `crates/ai/src/config.rs`, `crates/ai/tests/ai/evaluate.rs` and a decision test beside it
- SPEC §2.3, §6 (Float), §10.7; R464, R1563000

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An evaluation test: with a Float card above the seat's crystals in hand, a passed line that Floats F scores no lower than the same line with no Float card in hand; with no Float card in hand, every score is as before.
- [ ] A decision test: an Easy seat on 4 crystals, holding Drone Core IX and a 1-cost 1/1 against an empty board, ends its turn with crystals left, and next turn casts Drone Core IX.
- [ ] A decision test: with Drone Core X within reach and a free unit zone, the AI casts it.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` passes, and `cargo jackioh sweep stinkyscape-033 stinkyscape-034 stinkyscape-035 stinkyscape-036` shows more casts than the 2026-10-29 report; both numbers are in the pull request.

## Size and risks
Medium: one engine read, one weight and its pricing, three or four tests. Set too high, the weight makes the AI hoard mana instead of building a board; it applies only while a card is still out of reach, and the gate guards the rest. It changes how the AI plays, so the gate's games are its real test.

## Steps

0. **Baseline, before any edit.** `cargo jackioh sweep stinkyscape-033 stinkyscape-034 stinkyscape-035 stinkyscape-036 > /tmp/sweep-before.txt 2>&1`. Keep each card's rows per tier (drawn/games, affordable turns, plays). 1. **`script.rs`.** In `TriggerDef` add `pub float_cost: bool` with a doc line (R3695000: the trigger lowers its card's cost by its owner's Float). Set `float_cost: false` in `TriggerDef::new`. Beside `even_if_gone()` add `pub fn lowers_cost_on_float(mut self) -> TriggerDef { self.float_cost = true; self }`. Fuse (`subsystems/fuse.rs` ~1324) spreads `..trigger.clone()`, so a fused card keeps the flag: do not edit it.
2. **The three other literals** (`twice_forward.rs`, c064, c071): add `float_cost: false,` after `even_if_gone: false,`. Nothing else in those files.
3. **`float.rs`.** `float_reduces_cost` becomes `TriggerDef::new(..).with_when(..).lowers_cost_on_float()`; leave `float_lowers_tribute` alone (it cuts no cost). Add, with a doc comment citing R3695000:
   ```rust
   pub fn float_cuts_in_hand(state: &GameState, player: PlayerId, float: i32) -> Vec<(&CardInstance, i32)>
   ```
   `float <= 0` returns empty. Otherwise, for each card of `state.players[player].hand`, `n` = `crate::scripts::script_of(state, card).hand_triggers.iter().filter(|t| t.float_cost).count()` (the call `triggers::holder_of` makes); a card with `n > 0` is returned with the cut `float * n`, its `costMod` change (the price floors at 0, R1563000). 4. **`cross/float_cuts.rs` and `mod.rs`.** See Tests.
5. **`ai/config.rs`.** In `EvalWeights`, after `unspent_mana`, add a documented `pub float_discount: f64` (R3695000). Every test literal of `EvalWeights` uses `..AI_EVAL`, so none breaks.
6. **`duos.rs`.** `fn next_turn_mana` (~line 326) becomes `pub(crate) fn next_turn_mana`. Nothing else.
7. **`evaluate.rs`.** Add (import `float::float_cuts_in_hand` from `jackioh_engine` and `crate::duos::next_turn_mana`; `own_cost` is imported):
   ```rust
   /// R3695000: ...
   pub fn float_credit(state: &GameState, seat: PlayerId, float: i32, w: &EvalWeights) -> f64 {
       if w.float_discount == 0.0 || float <= 0 { return 0.0; }
       let cuts = float_cuts_in_hand(state, seat, float);
       if cuts.is_empty() { return 0.0; }
       let crystals = next_turn_mana(state, &state.players[seat]);
       let nearer: i32 = cuts.iter().filter_map(|(card, cut)| {
           let now = own_cost(state, card)?;           // unfloored; None for an X-cost card
           Some((now + cut - crystals).clamp(0, *cut))  // now + cut = the cost before this Float
       }).sum();
       w.float_discount * f64::from(nearer)
   }
   ```
   Why: a passed line's state is read after its turn ended, so the engine has already put the Float on the card's `costMod`; `own_cost + cut` is therefore the cost before the line's Float, exact even where the price floors. The credit is the crystals of the Float that fell on the distance still owed (cost before, less the crystals the seat has next turn: `next_turn_mana` reads the handicap, R180, and R844's lost refreshes), at most the Float. A card already in reach, or a crystal past the distance, earns nothing, so there is no hoarding past the need. Several Float cards sum, each its own distance.
8. **`simulate.rs` `passed_score`:** `line_score(..) - AI_EVAL.unspent_mana * f64::from(unspent) + float_credit(state, seat, unspent, &AI_EVAL)`. **`reply.rs` `replied_score`:** append `+ float_credit(end, seat, unspent, &AI_EVAL)` (`end` is the state right after the turn ended; `unspent` is 0 unless the line passed). Import it as each file imports its other `evaluate` items. The greedy baseline never reaches either function (`baselines.rs`, `skill.rs` call `evaluate(.., &GREEDY_EVAL)`), so it stays frozen; with no Float card in hand the credit is `0.0` and every score is as before.
9. **Tests in `ai/float_discount.rs`.** See Tests. Write the cast test (last bullet) **first** and run it on the code of steps 1–8.
10. **The second cause.** If the cast test fails: print `candidate_actions(&state, AI, Prices::NONE)` (is a `Play` of Drone Core X listed?), then `evaluate` before and after the cast (`simulate`, as `after_playing` in `slumber.rs`), then `decide`'s `reason` and `stats`. Suspects, in order: the play is not listed (the Battleship's three layers are one pile into one free unit zone, R1842000); the cast scores below the hand card it spends (`doomed_hand_card_value`, evaluate.rs ~542: `hand_card + hand_per_cost * min(cost, 6)` and `cost_shift`); the beam keeps another line. Fix it only if the fix is small, under `crates/ai/src`, and the test covers it. If it is not small, add no failing test and no `#[ignore]`: write what you found in the ruling's "Approximation" paragraph and in your final message.
11. **Spec.** `spec/rulings/R3695000.md`, modelled on `R3064000.md`: `id: R3695000`, a `title`, `cards: "#29, S #33, S #34, S #35, S #36, M #49.1; §2.3, §6.2, §9.9, R464, R766, R1563000, R2657002"`, `proven_in:` the two new test files. Body: what the AI now does, step 7's formula, what is not counted (deck cards, the enemy's hand, a card in reach, X-cost cards, Tribute Floats), the weight and what the gate and sweep read, and **Rejected**: a hand-written or build-found list of Float cards (#3130's lesson; the trigger marker reads what the engine registers, fused cards too); raising `hand_cost_cap` (moves every card's price and the frozen baseline); max instead of sum over cards; `MAX_MANA` as the reach (ignores Medium and Hard's crystals); a weight under `unspent_mana`. `spec/pending/3695.md`: one line, `**[[R3695000]] The AI Floats on purpose to bring a Float-discount card within reach (issue #3695, 2026-11-12)**: …`. `spec/09-architecture.md`: Grep `unspent mana at the end of the turn, the enemy's face damage next turn` (it must match once) and insert after "turn": `(each crystal a Float takes off a Float-discount card in its own hand that is still above its crystals next turn counts back, up to the cut still owed, [[R3695000]])`. README: three lines naming `float_credit`, `float_cuts_in_hand` and that `GREEDY_EVAL` keeps 0.
12. **Run the checks** (Done when), then the gate and the sweep again; put the sweep's before and after rows in the ruling's text (as R3064000 does with its gate numbers) and in your final message.

## Tests

`crates/cards/tests/cross/float_cuts.rs` (`use jackioh_engine::float::float_cuts_in_hand; use jackioh_engine::testkit::*; use super::scenario;`):

`crates/ai/tests/ai/float_discount.rs` (`use jackioh_ai::*; use jackioh_engine::testkit::*; use super::support::{AI, HUMAN, act, close, register_cards};`; copy the style of `slumber.rs` and `surface.rs`). Helpers: `INERT = "stand-in (9) 1/1"` (never affordable), `DC_IX = "stinkyscape-035"`, `DC_X = "stinkyscape-036"`, `SIX = "stand-in (6) Spell"` (6 crystals, no Float trigger); `on_turn(turn, hand, mana)` = `register_cards(); scenario(json!({"seed": "ai-float-discount", "active": "p1", "turn": turn, "p1": {"hand": hand, "mana": mana, "library": [INERT; 4]}, "p2": {"hand": [INERT], "library": [INERT; 4]}})).state().clone()` (turn 9 gives p1 four crystals); `passed(s)` = `terminal_score(s, AI, 9, &create_node_counter(10, None), Prices::NONE)`; `ended(s)` = `act(s, AI, &ActionBody::EndTurn)`. `line_score` is the hand eval at `LEARNED_REACH = Finalists`, so these sums are exact.

- `r3695000_an_easy_seat_with_drone_core_ix_and_a_one_drop_ends_with_crystals_left_and_casts_it_next_turn`: `on_turn(7, [DC_IX, "stand-in (1) 1/1"], 4)`; `play_ai_turn(&s, AI, &mut AiOptions::new(create_rng("ai-float-ix", 0)))`; assert `state.players[AI].turn_log.unspent_at_end >= Some(2)` and `effective_cost(&state, card, CostOptions::default()) <= 4` for the Drone Core; if `state.active == HUMAN`, `act(.., HUMAN, &ActionBody::EndTurn)`; `play_ai_turn` again; assert one of its `actions` is a `Play` of the Drone Core's id.
